sub_palette: germanic (frankish) backbone + east_asian (japonic) overlay (cross-family blend, Germanic-leaning)

blend.backbone: germanic (frankish / Old High German register: the kuning/herizogo and the truhtin-treuwa lord-vassal bond, High German shift th>d/d>t/k>ch-hh, -o/-i endings, dithematic Hilde-/Gund-/-ric names)
blend.overlay: east_asian (japonic: the island land of -yama/-gawa and the -no-fields, the jinja shrine-folk and the clan-villages, the daimyo-and-samurai houses, mora-timed open CV speech, honorific X-no-Y linking, SOV agglutinative grammar)
blend.lean: Germanic-heavy - a Frankish feudal war-aristocracy enthroned over the Japanese island-clans: the Frankish lord-and-vassal bond fused with the samurai loyalty-code, two warrior feudalisms made one. The Frankish herizogo and his sworn vassals rule from the burg; the daimyo-houses and the shrine-folk of the islands serve beneath as the sworn bushi of the realm.

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_01 Thiodmark (Germanic) x BASE_08 Yamatai-base (Japonic / East Asian). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Germanic base = Clanhold, Japonic-Japanese base = Civilized, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Hinogard is Civilized (feudal). Concept: a Frankish war-aristocracy that conquered the Japanese island-clans and set up as feudal lords over them - the Frankish lord-and-vassal bond (truhtin/treuwa) meeting the samurai's loyalty-code (shujun/chugi), two warrior feudalisms fused ('the fire-island realm'). Backbone = Germanic (frankish / Old High German: the ruling war-aristocracy, the herizogo/kuning register, the High German consonant shift, dithematic names); overlay/substrate = Japonic (the island land of -yama and -gawa, the daimyo-houses and the bushi retainers, the jinja shrine-folk and the clan-villages, mora-timed open-syllable speech, the X-no-Y honorific linking). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Old High German (Frankish) and Japanese registers (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents - Frankish reflexes PRIMARY (family_germanic theonym_ancestors, the frankish column), Japonic NATIVE-kami variants SECONDARY (family_east_asian theonym_sets.japonic, treated exactly as Yamataian treats them - wholly native kami, never the Sinitic forms, never real Shinto kami). PROVISIONAL: alignment (Lawful/Neutral) is a per-hybrid design choice pending the alignment pass - the Frankish feudal oath-order and the samurai bushido way both read Lawful (the sworn lord-vassal bond, the disciplined warrior-code), but an older island layer of the wild kami and the mountain-oni reads Neutral. Register choice: Germanic-base hybrids default to the GOTHIC/continental reflexes, but Hinogard deliberately takes the FRANKISH (OHG) reflexes because the feudal lord-vassal bond is the Frankish/Merovan inheritance (the parallel to the daimyo-samurai relation) - flag for Jedidiah if a uniform Germanic register is wanted instead. [UPDATE 2026-06-27: all human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic (per-hybrid alignment restriction removed). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are now English (or an approved foreign term); conlang titles moved to ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue. Deities unchanged: canonical Agrippan pantheon via the per-family morph method.]

phonology.palette: Germanic (Frankish / Old High German) backbone - root-initial stress, sharp stops, the High German consonant shift (th>d, d>t, k>ch/hh; truhtin, herizogo), w>w/wu, endings -o/-i, dithematic compounding - meeting a Japonic overlay: open CV moras (only coda -n), the five vowels a i u e o, pitch accent, no consonant clusters, rendaku (sequential voicing) in compounds, the X-no-Y honorific linking and the -yama/-gawa/-no toponyms. Per the CSV: softened consonants (the OHG shift and the cluster-free Japonic moras) over a rigid rhythm (heavy Germanic root-stress meeting strict mora-timing); grammar shifts toward SOV with agglutinative case-particles and strong-verb stems (the Japonic substrate carried on Frankish strong stems). Theophoric on the Frankish reflexes (Dulro-, Erlant-) with Japonic native-kami variants (-no-kami, -hime).
phonology.phonotactics: Frankish CVC with OHG clusters (st, sk, hr, kn) and the shifted stops (ch/hh, t, d), root-initial stress, dithematic compounds; the Japonic substrate strips clusters into open CV moras and adds rendaku voicing and the -no- linking particle; dithematic Frankish burg-names over -yama / -gawa / -shiro island toponyms.

sound_changes: Japonic open CV moras filtered into Frankish syllable shape: drop final root-vowels and impose codas/clusters (kawa>gaw, yama>jam, mori>mor, minato>minat); the mora-rhythm bends to a single heavy root-initial Frankish stress
the High German consonant shift reaches the Japonic roots: t>d/z, k>ch/hh, intervocalic stops soften (tetsu>dezz, machi>mach, sato>sad); Frankish stops t/d/ch held in the lean words
Japonic toponymic morphemes adapt to Frankish form: -no (field) > -an/-en clipped, -yama > -jam/-am, -gawa > -gaw with retained rendaku voicing, -shiro > -shir
rendaku (sequential voicing) is kept as the one audible Japonic signature in compounds, but Frankish clusters override the no-cluster rule (kn, hr, st, br permitted; shima>shimb, seto>sezt)

Frankish-sourced kin/quality/abstract/war roots take OHG shape unchanged-in-spirit (-o/-i endings, mihhil, swarz, isarn), supplying the prestige register; short Japonic roots gain a Frankish coda or -o
fusion_rules.source_tilt: island/land/terrain/material/staple words from Japonic roots (the island substrate works the land and sea: the -yama/-gawa/-no land, the rice and silk and iron-ore); kin-line/quality/abstract/rule/war words from Frankish roots (the OHG ruling register: mihhil, swarz, isarn, the truhtin-bond); every chosen root is then run through the one Frankish-shaped sound-law so the split is inaudible

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Japonic island/land/material roots + Frankish (OHG) rule/kin/quality roots, all run through one Frankish-shaped sound-law (clusters imposed, mora-rhythm bent to root-initial stress, High German shift reaching the Japonic stems, rendaku kept as the lone substrate signature); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline. One language - Frankish-shaped, Japonic-substrated - not a slash list.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Frankish ruling house keeps a dithematic lineage-name and -ingen (descendant of); the Japonic island-clans keep the uji / -shi clan-name borne first with the -no- linking (X no Y) and the house-suffix -ke; the throne fuses both - a herizogo of a Frankish dithematic line who also holds a Japonic clan-seat.
morphology.compounding_rule: Frankish dithematic ([quality|feature](stem) + element: Isarn-burg, iron-fort; Hrod-heim, glory-home) layered over Japonic feature-compounds with rendaku ([quality]+type: Kuro-yama black-mountain, Aka-shiro red-castle -> rendaku -gawa): the capital Hino-gard (the fire-island stronghold), Hilde-shiro (the war-castle of the Hilde-line).

title_ladder.government: feudal (a Frankish war-aristocracy over the Japanese island-clans: the kuning and his herizogo-dukes at the crown, the grafo-counts over the provinces, the truhtin-lords and their sworn vassals; the daimyo-houses and their bushi retainers serve beneath as the sworn warriors of the realm, the kannushi shrine-priesthood and the village-folk beneath them)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Frankish (OHG) feudal ladder, ascending, with the Japonic clan co-titles beneath. Truhtin (sworn lord; *druhtinaz, the lord-of-the-war-band) barony over a Truhti; Marcha-grafo (march-count) march; Grafo (count) county over a Grafscaf; Herizogo (war-leader, duke; *harja-tugon) duchy over a Herizogtuom; Furisto (the first, prince) principality; Kuning (king) kingdom over a Kuningrihhi; Keisar (emperor < Caesar) empire over the Keisarrihhi. The conquered island-clans keep their Daimyo (great-house lord, sworn as the duke's vassals), Shugo (province-governor) and Jito (estate-lord) beneath the Frankish crown; the bushi (samurai) are the sworn retainers, the kannushi (shrine-priest) stands outside the ladder. Rank titles fuse the real Old High German (Frankish) and Japanese registers (allowed).
title_ladder.heir: Kuning-barn (the king's child; the heir) / Yotsugi (the designated heir, Japonic)
title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH (or an approved commonly-known foreign term where set in 'ruler'). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: the Frankish ruling stock carry a dithematic name + -ingen lineage; the Japonic island-clans carry a clan-name (uji/-shi) borne first with the given name (X no Y); the ruling line fuses both - a dithematic Frankish given-name over a held island clan-seat. Order given-first for the Frankish lords, clan-first for the island-clans.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Frankish war-aristocracy keep OHG dithematic names (Hilde-, Gund-, Hrod-, -ric, -hari, -ramn); the Japanese island-clans keep their clan + given names (Kurokawa no Takeshi) on the native stock.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Frankish devotional on the morphed canon-reflexes (the Dulro- 'sun-' and Erlant- 'war-iron-' elements): Dulro-hari (Dulro's-army), Erlant-ric (war-iron-ruler); the Japonic substrate keeps the native-kami devotion + an element (-maru child/blade, Take- valor, Kami- divine): Takebimaru, names honoring Terashi-no-kami.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Frankish reflexes PRIMARY (family_germanic theonym_ancestors, the frankish column: the High German shift th>d, d>t), Japonic variants SECONDARY and treated exactly as Yamataian treats them: wholly NATIVE kami (family_east_asian theonym_sets.japonic), NOT borrowed from the Sinitic forms and never real Shinto kami. ALIGNMENT IS PROVISIONAL (Lawful/Neutral): the Frankish feudal oath-order and the samurai bushido way both read Lawful (the sworn lord-vassal bond, the disciplined warrior-code, the kami of sun and blade and ancestors), but an older island layer reads Neutral (the wild kami, the mountain-oni, the local hearth- and grove-spirits). Both treatments given below pending Jedidiah's alignment decision (see gdd-culture-emergence-and-territory.md open questions).
religion.the_one: Aiterno (Frankish < *Aiternaz; Japonic Takami-no-kami) - the distant Ancient One, the High-Heaven One above the lesser powers, honored not petitioned

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Dulro (Jp. Terashi-no-kami) - the sun, the just brightness, right-rule
sample_deity_renames.Orlandus: Erlant (Jp. Hagane-no-kami) - iron, the blade-oath, war
sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Giando (Jp. Iwane-no-kami) - the enduring earth, the rock-root mountain
sample_deity_renames.Realta: Rialda (Jp. Megumi-hime) - the mother, mercy, healing

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Aiterno foremost, Dulro the just-bright, Erlant of the sworn war, Rialda the merciful, Giando the steadfast earth (and their kami faces: Terashi-no-kami, Hagane-no-kami) - and names the Chaotic powers warded and unworshipped (the Frankish ungiwiht/devils, the wild oni); the sworn lord-vassal oath and the bushido way are the social ideal
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: ancestral and local - the deified war-dead of the ruling house and the senzo (forebears) of the clans, the hearth- and grove-spirits and the island kami of mountain, shrine and field; the great powers invoked at the grove-temple and the jinja situationally rather than worshipped wholesale
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon, and names the Lawful powers - and Aiterno - as the tyrant-gods to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as ungiwiht (Frankish monsters/devils) or as fierce kami and oni (Japonic), keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Marach the War-Brand (Jp. Takebi-no-kami the War-Flame); Vacidus -> Wachid the Unmaker (Jp. Utsuro-no-kami the Devouring Void); Lusanto -> Lusando the Hoard-Worm (Jp. Kogane-Orochi the gold hoard-serpent).

clergy_ladder.9: Altisto-priast (eldest priest of the realm) / Saishu

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Harug (Frankish grove-temple) or Jinja (Japonic shrine) of [power]: 'the Harug of Dulro', 'the Jinja of Terashi-no-kami', within its torii and sacred grove.
religion.saints_pattern: the deified war-dead of the ruling house (honored at the howe and the grove) and the great ancestors and fallen heroes enshrined as kami (the eirei) at the clan jinja; 'the kami [name]'.

holy_symbol_motifs.Dulro: a sun-disc over a crossed sword (the kami-face: a rising sun-disc above a mirror and blade)
holy_symbol_motifs.Erlant: an iron sword crossed with a spear (the kami-face: a bare blade before a torii)
holy_symbol_motifs.Giando: the green island-hill beneath the standing stones and the sacred mountain
